![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203245/assets/a9c863e0cdb9788e06c527e17207e87ba2281ab21c9bd0836009ca518a15631a.png)

Given the triangle above, find the length of $\overset{―}{AB}$ rounded to one decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
For an angle $\theta $ in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{adjacent leg}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$

- $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}}$

Notice that we are given the length of the leg $\overset{―}{BC}$ adjacent to the given angle $∠C$ and wish to find the length of the leg $\overset{―}{AB}$ opposite $∠C.$

The trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite leg to the adjacent leg is *tangent*. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠C) & =\frac{\text{opposite leg}}{\text{adjacent leg}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({56}^{∘}) & =\frac{AB}{9} \\ AB & =9\operatorname{tan}⁡({56}^{∘}).\end{aligned}
$$

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =9\operatorname{tan}⁡({56}^{∘}) \\  & =9(1.482\,56…) \\  & =13.343\,04… \\  & ≈13.3,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
